articleTitle: Rethinking the electricity system of the Island of Guernsey
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: Globally, the way energy is generated, distributed and used is changing. A methodology for transitioning existing electricity systems is being introduced, using an island as a case study. The Island of Guernsey, which includes approximately 63,000 inhabitants, has a current electricity demand of 397 GWh/year. Their primary supply source is an interconnector from France via Jersey, which is supported by on-island dispatchable oil-fired generators. These generators are nearing their end-of-life, while there is an increasing desire to electrify heating and transport. Hence, the States of Guernsey require an electricity strategy that enables long-term planning and investment, and meets their policy objectives. Guernsey's future electricity demand was modelled alongside six possible supply pathways, each with a different mix of renewable, traditional and interconnector technologies. Utilising digital twin software, the detailed energy, cost and emission impacts over the period to 2050 were determined. Through an iterative stakeholder consultation process, a primary pathway was selected for the electricity strategy, and further sensitivity and refinement analyses were conducted. The study concludes that the Island of Guernsey can achieve its policy objectives through capital investment in renewable generation and an additional interconnector, and that doing so is more economical than continuing with business-as-usual.

articleTitle: Analysis of interactive oscillation modes for LCC-HVDC system in single-infeed mode and split-connection mode
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: There exist single-infeed mode and split-connection mode for Yongfu HVDC project in China. Differences of system stability characteristic between the two connection modes are unclear. In this paper, a small signal dynamic model of LCC-HVDC system is established. By means of eigenvalue analysis and participation factor analysis, weakly damped interactive oscillation modes reflecting the interaction between the inverter-side control system and receiving AC girds are identified, which may be the key modes dominating the system stability. On this basis, variation characteristics of interactive oscillation modes in two connection modes are investigated by the analysis of eigenvalue loci with varying DC voltage control parameter under different SCR conditions. The theoretical analysis and simulation results manifest that, in the single-infeed mode, the system stability is dominated by the common-mode. In the split-connection mode, when two receiving AC grid strengths are identical/ similar, the stability characteristic of the two poles are similar, and there is an extra anti-mode to further weaken the system stability, compared to the corresponding single-infeed mode. When two receiving AC grid strengths differ greatly, the stability characteristics of the two poles are relatively independent.

articleTitle: The effect of increasing solar photovoltaic generation on medium-term net-load forecasting
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: The amount of distributed solar photovoltaic (PV) energy generation is increasing rapidly and often occurs behind the meters (BTM) used by grid operators to measure demand for electricity. As a result, operators must now forecast the net-load. Accurate medium-term electrical power system load forecasting is important for optimising power system operation. The PV generation is weather dependent, and its interaction with the grid increases the variability of the net-load which decreases net-load forecast accuracy. This paper investigates the effect of BTM PV generation on medium term net-load forecasting accuracy, and how the use of past net-load data, irradiance data and disaggregation influence the decrease in accuracy. Machine learning methods were utilised to demonstrate the impact: an established load forecasting multiple linear regression (MLR) benchmark, a newly proposed net-load forecasting MLR benchmark built upon the load forecasting benchmark, and deep learning methods. The results show that the rate of increase in error for load forecasting methods increases as the BTM PV generation is increased. As a result, the adverse impact of BTM PV on net-load forecast accuracy may be greater than anticipated. Finally, weather data, including irradiance forecasts with large error can still be used to improve net-load forecast accuracy.

articleTitle: Challenges and solutions in the operation of varied energy integrations with HVDC transmission connecting continents
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: Ambitious target to reach net zero emission and related initiatives across the globe has motivated grid integration of bulk nonfossil fuel-based power generation sources, energy storage systems with the help of power electronic converters. The replacement of synchronous machines (SMs) and their stabilizing control mechanisms, e.g., governor, automatic voltage regulator, and power system stabilizer by power electronic converter-based generation, has transformed the conventional power system to the so-called low-inertia paradigm, characterized by the significant reduction of rotational inertia in the AC grid. One such integration of varied energy sources like solar PV, Battery Energy Storage System of large capacity integration through HVDC network facilitating power transmission over long distances (can be connecting continents to achieve net zero or carbon neutrality) is considered in this paper. This kind of integration brings along several new challenges and opportunities employing High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) transmission system in the grid operation. The challenges and solution in the operation of such an integration is presented in this paper and is demonstrated with the help of simulation study employing PSCAD / EMTDC software.

articleTitle: Increasing power transfer capability of existing overhead lines using six-phase technology
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: To deliver the UK's Net-Zero commitment, the GB Transmission Network must be capable of transporting sufficient clean electrical energy to the networks that distribute electricity to the final consumers. Future electrification of heat and transport significantly raises demand, which imposes thermal challenges on the power transfer capability of existing transmission feeders, especially on windy winter days when the sources are remote from the demand. For environmental and planning reasons, construction of new overhead lines is problematic and where possible upgrading of existing substations and lines is preferred. This paper revisits six-phase (6Φ) technology, and discusses the advantages and challenges of transforming an existing three-phase (3Φ) double-circuit 400kV line into a six-phase (6Φ) feeder operating at a higher line-neutral voltage. The emphasis of the paper is system security, protection, insulation coordination and cost effectiveness, but mitigation of the challenges expected with such a radical proposal are also discussed.

articleTitle: Developing requirements for future electrical machine manufacture to achieve a net zero future
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: This paper summarises work done by the EPSRC Future Electrical Machines Manufacturing (FEMM) Hub on its technology roadmap. It outlines the challenge, approach and progress to-date in linking the role of electrical machines in the journey to net zero with specific research challenges. It has been based on a net zero CO2 emissions future as the end point, and explores what developments in electrical machines manufacture will be needed to get there. Given the likely role of electrical machines in a net zero future it seems natural that a roadmap in this area seeks to understand and describe what this means in terms of electrical machines and how they need to be made in future. This work sits alongside other roadmaps, focused on the journey to net zero in various industry sectors. It provides unique additional insight by focusing specifically on machines and by considering needs and implications across sectors from power generation to surface and air transportation. As a research hub, FEMM Hub's primary intent has been to use this approach as a basis for identifying the early TRL research needs. Inevitably however the problem has many facets and several findings extend into likely public policy and industrial transformation.

articleTitle: Forward-aggregation backward-identification based power system frequency response model
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: To improve the performance of traditional system frequency response (SFR) models, establishing a SFR model with low-order, high adaptability and accuracy becomes an important technical pathway. The paper proposes a forward-aggregation backward-identification (FABI) based SFR model, which comprehensively takes account of the prime movers and governors of non-reheat steam turbines, reheat steam turbines and hydraulic turbines, as well as various frequency responses of renewable energy sources and loads. Firstly, FABI SFR configures the proportions of generating elements in different types existing in a power system and the equivalent regulation parameters of governors. Then, it aggregates the physical parameters of prime movers in different types. Lastly, by comparing to frequency trajectories simulated from a detailed time-domain IEEE 10-machine 39-bus model in PSCAD platform, FABI SFR identifies key parameters of inertia, damping coefficient and speed regulation time constant, which is crucial for enhancing model accuracy. Case studies are carried out to analyse the FABI SFR performance, verifying that FABI SFR can be readily adopted in a specific power system and improve the prediction accuracy of the grid frequency response.

articleTitle: Stable operating area evaluation of grid-forming MMC-HVDC system with renewable energy integration
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: This paper presents a method to obtain the operating area of the grid-forming modular multilevel converter based high voltage direct current (MMC-HVDC) system with photovoltaic and hydroelectric power integration. First, the steady-state mathematical model and small-signal model of the whole system are established and the stable operation constraints are analysed. Then the method to obtain the operating area of the system is proposed and the operating areas of MMC-HVDC under different shortcircuit ratio (SCR) are analysed. The results show that with the decrease of SCR, the stable operation area is mainly reduced due to the enhancement of voltage constraints, and the feasible range of reactive power of MMC-HVDC decreases. However, when SCR increases to 5, the system cannot transmit rated power due to small-signal stability constraint, which means that the voltage-frequency (VF) droop control is not suitable for strong AC system. Finally, the accuracy of the theoretical analysis is proved by time-domain simulation results.

articleTitle: Probabilistic modelling for connection studies
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: Conventional network planning approach for transmission networks in Great Britain (GB) is deterministic, which looks at a "worst-case" scenario. However, this methodology was developed when the network was dominated by large, fossil fuel generators, feeding a passive network. As the country is moving toward Net Zero with more and more intermittent renewables, flexible demand and energy storage, the level of unpredictability rises. This paper proposes to develop a probabilistic approach to network planning and connection studies. A capacity factor based probabilistic model for a year-duration profile will be proposed, representing behaviour of energy storage systems, hydropower generation and pumped storage. It is aimed to inform decision-making as well as yielding a more efficient development and connection of renewable generation and flexibility assets.

articleTitle: Impact of POD decomposition orders on reduced-order modeling for transformer temperature computation
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: The finite element method is widely used in fields such as heat transfer for its ability to provide complete and accurate solutions to physical fields. However, in engineering applications, a finite element method may suffer from slow computational speed, making it impractical for real-time scenarios. The Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) method, on the other hand, extracts the dominant features from high-dimensional data and represents them in a lower-dimensional form, allowing for a more efficient approximation of the original data. By combining POD with the finite element method, it becomes possible to simulate physical fields rapidly while maintaining computational accuracy. Considering the influence of different orders of basis vectors in POD decomposition on the simulation of physical fields, this study constructs a simplified thermal conduction model of a transformer core. By comparing the simulation accuracy and computational time for different orders of basis vectors, the optimal order for this model is determined, and the reasons for decreased accuracy at higher orders are analyzed. The research findings reveal the factors leading to the degradation of simulation results by high-order basis vectors in POD decomposition, contributing to the search for appropriate orders of basis vectors.

articleTitle: Batteries in wind-dominated areas of network: solution or problem? A Scottish case study
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: This work investigates the hypothesis: “grid-connected batteries will not export energy at times of high wind energy availability in Scotland, nor add to network congestion.” The likely rational behaviour of a short-duration (two-hour) battery, engaged in trades in the wholesale electricity market in Great Britain is simulated, for three case study periods during 2022, using scenarios of different trading strategies and foresight of market price. In the scenarios yielding highest revenues, times of battery import and export actions are compared with times of Scottish wind energy availability and transmission network congestion. Results show such a battery will continue to trade, both importing and exporting, during periods of high wind availability, conditions under which network congestion is common. Thus, the possibility that short-duration batteries may add to network congestion by exporting during periods of high wind availability must be allowed for by network planners, the system operator and the regulator. Market, network and / or regulatory solutions are needed.

articleTitle: Optimal power production analysis for bifacial photovoltaic units using different albedos framed by energy-economic and environmental assessment
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: The aim of this work is to optimize the energy yield of bifacial solar modules by using different reflective materials, considering the ecological and economic effects. For this purpose, measurements were carried out on a bifacial module on a laboratory scale as well as simulations for a solar system with an installed capacity of 763.2 kWp. For the environmental assessment, the grey energy and CO2 equivalent emissions of the materials were offset against the CO2 emissions avoided by the increased solar energy production. For the economic evaluation, the additional costs were weighed against the additional income.The base surfaces concrete and arable soil as well as the reflective materials white pebbles and geotextile mats in the colors white and grey were tested. In addition, the increase in efficiency using bifacial PV modules compared to monofacial PV modules was evaluated for the respective materials. By using white geotextile mats as a reflective surface, the energy production was maximized and increased by 10 % compared to the baseline situation. Compared to the use of monofacial PV modules, the use of white geotextile mats leads to an increase in energy yield of almost 14 %. If the reflective materials are replaced every three years, a permanent positive economic return can be achieved for this most energy-efficient variant after just 7 years. The use of white pebbles, on the other hand, is already profitable after four years under the same circumstances. In the ecological evaluation, the white geotextile mat performs significantly better. Over a period of 20 years, up to 100 tons of CO2 can be saved in Brazil, while the use of white pebbles only saves 63 tons. Thus, the use of white geotextile mats with replacement of the material every three years can be seen as an economically as well as ecologically sensible measure for the construction of the solar system.

articleTitle: Multi-physics modeling method of ONAN transformer temperature field for digital twin application
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: With the increasing electrical load on power grids, the issue of overheating in oil-immersed transformers during operation has become a critical concern. Traditional methods of temperature measurement used to assess the temperature distribution of transformer oil are insufficient in providing a comprehensive representation of the entire oil circulation system. To tackle this challenge, digital twin technology has emerged as a promising approach for analyzing and evaluating transformer maintenance requirements. Therefore, an architecture is presented in this article for the application of digital twin technology to transformers, emphasizing the importance of multiphysical field simulation in constructing an accurate digital twin model. A methodology is then outlined for developing a digital twin for oil-immersed, self-cooled (ONAN) transformers, with a specific focus on constructing a multi-physics digital twin simulation model to accurately capture the complete temperature distribution of transformer oil. In this model, an innovative approach is proposed, drawing inspiration from the concept of oil conservators.

articleTitle: Diversified flexible queue management: analysis of Great Britain distribution network hosting capacity with diversification of generation and demand
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: Achieving net zero ambition in the UK relies on the integration of renewable energy sources and storage (RES) within the Great Britain power network. These RES are connected within the distribution network at specific locations that favour maximum generation, such as locations with high wind resource (for wind farms) or high solar irradiance (for solar farm). Such geographic dependence increases the loading at specific points within the distribution network. When evaluating connection requests for generation and storage technologies to the network, traditionally the rated capacity of the generation units is utilised to assess headroom. The high volume of applications and the reserving of the full rated capacity for each applicant has resulted in significant queues as the network companies build reinforcement to meet capacity demand. However, it is known that the RES are unlikely to always operate at their rated capacity due to availability of resources or market conditions for operation. Therefore, in real-time operation there is often network capacity available. This paper investigates the feasibility to utilise this available capacity by considering the diversity in seasonal and market operating conditions of the generation and demand technologies. The Diversified Flexible Queue Management innovation project (DFQM) seeks to investigate the viability of data intelligence to drive network operation and adaptive management of distribution connections queue. It will assess the diversity of customer loads and the flexibility of their generation assets, aimed to estimate real-time capacity as a tool for identifying opportunities for additional customers to connect to the network, enabling speedier connection times.

articleTitle: A power management system for interconnected AC islanded microgrids using back-to-back converter
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: Islanded AC microgrids are mini-power grids formed by assembling distributed generation sources, energy storage systems and loads. They are reliable and can operate at different voltages and frequencies to meet the requirements of the load. Interconnected Islanded Microgrids consist of multiple islanded microgrids interconnected to improve power system availability and stability, control flexibility, resiliency and reserve capacity. Islanded microgrids can be interconnected using back-to-back power converters to decouple connecting frequencies whose active and reactive power control can be done wirelessly and autonomously under a low communication link. This paper proposes a novel structure and control strategy using back-to-back converters and power transformers to interconnect multiple islanded AC microgrids to a global AC bus. Microgrids and global bus can utilise their resources to improve their operation and benefits. The control strategy uses a frequency signalling mechanism to limit the power demand of individual global converters and adjusts its droop coefficients accordingly and in proportion to deviation in frequency. The global droop controllers of the global connecting converters receive information about the status of the frequencies of individual microgrids using a low bandwidth communication link to enhance network power flow. MATLAB/Simulink results validate the performance of the proposed structure and control strategy.

articleTitle: Optimisation strategies to reduce renewables curtailment using transportable energy storage systems
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: Increasing shares of renewable energy sources in power systems worldwide have led to increased renewable curtailment due to network and/or stability limitations. Energy storage systems, both stationary and mobile, are widely proposed as a promising solution for reducing such curtailment. The paper presents a detailed analysis of renewable energy curtailment, taking the case study of a future Irish grid scenario, to identify the prospects of transportable energy storage systems (TESS). A combined unit commitment optimal power flow formulation has been developed to evaluate the locational curtailment from all renewable sources. The study establishes a baseline understanding of the locations and durations of renewable curtailment, providing insights on short-term/long-term TESS relocation, along with short/long distance movement possibilities, paving the way for optimal sizing and management of TESS units.

articleTitle: DC fault protection for offshore wind farms connected to MVDC systems
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: In this paper, the fault characteristics of the medium voltage DC (MVDC) systems considering different fault protection schemes are studied. The fault protection of an offshore MVDC network is considered together with the configuration of the protection equipment, DC transformers, and the onshore MVDC stations. Different protection schemes considering DC circuit breakers (DCCBs) and DC switches (DCSs) are implemented. In addition to a half-bridge (HB) submodule based modular multilevel converter (MMC), the application of a full-bridge (FB) submodule based MMC as the onshore station for DC fault protection is also assessed. Dual active bridge (DAB) and single active bridges (SAB) are studied and the impacts of the medium voltage side DC capacitor of the DAB on DC fault current are investigated. Simulation results confirm that the SAB+FB-MMC+DCS scheme provides a promising solution for the MVDC system for offshore wind power transmission.

articleTitle: Energy reduction actions to meet international maritime organisation (IMO) 2030 and impacts from introduction of electrical systems changes and considerations for power quality and harmonics
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: This paper will look at the steps towards a greener future for the shipping industry, including grey ships, commercial vessels and ports, and why the IMO 2030 and 2050 targets have been established. As operators of maritime platforms and port facilities move to meet lower emission standards, required by IMO2030, a number of solutions are being implemented or considered to meet these targets. The IMO initial strategy for reduction of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions is challenging ships and port operators alike and it is these end users who need to find, develop and integrate more energy-efficient solutions to meet GHG targets for both 2030 and 2050 targets These solutions include the greater use of LED technology to reduce lighting loads as well as the increased use of Variable Frequency Drives (VFD) and variable speed drives (VSD) to reduce motor loads on-board vessels. Port facilities likewise are building additional electrical power systems to allow for increased use of shore connections and HV cold ironing facilities for IEP vessels. This presentation will identify some of the concerns that operators need to be aware of when implementing energy reduction solutions using VFD's, LED's etc. and for operators with solutions already in place - how do they meet the requirements imposed by class societies such as LR, DNV etc. to keep Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) under control and meeting practical applications on vessels.

articleTitle: Passive-regulated DC microgrid for rural electrification: an assessment from a design for localisation approach
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: Low voltage DC microgrids can provide reliable, safe and efficient energy distribution for photovoltaic-battery systems. When used in a rural electrification context, these systems can be implemented either by using commercial off-the-shelf DC-DC converters or, most commonly, by using custom application-specific converters. These components do not usually allow local repair and maintenance, causing issues when failures occur. This paper presents a study case for the development of DC-DC power converters based on the Design for Localisation approach, that aims to design a product for local manufacture, use, repair and end-of-life processing, whilst considering the production process availability and the context of the local geographic area. In a rural electrification context, the Design for Localisation methodology makes it possible to use local skills and capabilities, contributing to the reduction of costs and time to repair, increased reliability and overall sustainable development of the community. The case study is based on a 24 V passive-regulated DC microgrid operating in the Brazilian Amazon, which currently operates using commercial off-the-shelf equipment and was developed as an alternative for remote electrification to reduce demand for household-scale diesel generators, commonly used in the community. The 3 Design for Localisation rules are applied to design a DC-DC power converter to substitute the commercial battery charge controllers that are used to control the PV generation and to form the microgrid. The proposed design is evaluated against the Design for Localisation criteria to show the feasibility of the design and establish the next steps required for implementation.

articleTitle: Design of an outer-translator flux switching linear generator for use in a heaving wave energy converter
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: This study discusses the design and optimisation of an outer-translator H-type flux switching permanent magnet linear generator for integration into a wave energy converter. The stator of the proposed electrical machine consists of six H-Type modules, each sandwiched by two permanent magnets (PMs). The translator is a toothed iron structure integrated into a heaving buoy wave energy converter. The buoy configuration is described prior to a basic hydrodynamic model being used to specify the parameters of a 2.4kW average power demonstrator generator. The electrical machine is optimised employing the Taguchi optimisation method with the aim of improving the thrust force and efficiency and lowering the force ripple. 2D finite element analysis is used to give thrust force, back emf, cogging force and magnetic flux density distributions of the optimised generator. Finally, the results are scaled to give a tubular design for the target wave energy converter.

articleTitle: Second harmonics reduction strategies for power converters in flexible interconnected distribution network
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: Flexible interconnected distribution network based on power electronics technology can greatly improve the system control flexibility and the system operation reliability, which has gradually become the future distribution network development trend. However, the distributed access of power electronic resources leads to harmonics injection, which affects the quality of electric energy for distribution network. The second harmonics caused by single-phase inverter is a serious problem, which will reduce system efficiency and lifetime. In order to reduce the harmonics, adjusting the control strategy of power converter is a simple and effective method. From the point of transfer impedance, this paper takes a deep research on the reduction of second harmonics. The generating mechanism of the second harmonics is deeply analyzed and revealed first. Then, the voltage and current double closed-loop control is analyzed and the inductor ripple current is found to be the significant cause. According to the derived conclusions, an hamonics reduction strategy is proposed to suppress the input second harmonic current. A 1500VA converter is built on MATLAB/Simulink and the obtained simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: DC fault ride-through for wind power integration via MMC-HVDC based on precise control of energy storage configured inside wind farm
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: The modular multilevel converter-based high voltage direct current (MMC-HVDC) overhead lines transmission scheme is the preferred option for wind power integration, though it is susceptible to DC faults. To ensure the connection of a wind farm (WF) to the grid during DC faults, this paper proposes a coordinated control strategy for DC fault ride-through (FRT) based on the energy storage system configured inside the WF for wind power integration through a bipolar MMC-HVDC. In the case of an instantaneous DC fault, the non-fault pole is regulated to operate at full power state to maximise wind power transmission. The exceedance of available wind power outputs over the transmission capacity of the non-fault pole is then accurately allocated to the internal energy storage units (ESUs) of wind generators (WGs) in order to ensure the power balance of the system and reduce the state of charge variance of ESUs as soon as possible. In order to reduce the energy capacities of ESUs required to store the excessive wind power in the event of a permanent DC fault, the method of step-by-step removing WGs is adopted to ensure the system power remaining balanced when the internal ESUs of the disconnected WGs are out of operation. The model is developed and carried out on the PSCAD/EMTDC simulation platform to verify the effectiveness of the proposed control strategies.

articleTitle: Modelling asymmetrical HVDC transfer network for multi-vendor-multi-terminal interoperability
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: To accommodate the need for offshore Multi-Vendor-Multi-Terminal (MVMT) bipolar High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) transmission grids to transfer massive wind power, an analytical model is developed to characterise the asymmetry in the transfer network. By introducing a generic representation of transfer conductance matrix, this model can characterize the behaviour of MVMT-HVDC schemes with hybrid of bipolar and monopole sections for assessment and future design. The accuracy of the model is validated by case studies of two applications with MATLAB/Simulink, namely predicting small-signal impedance of an HVDC grid with measurements of standalone components and indexing the security domain of operating point. This method will result in practice in a higher availability of the DC system than would otherwise be the case; offering new options for practical network operation and outage/ fault management.

articleTitle: Control of grid-forming VSC during symmetrical and asymmetrical ac faults
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: A grid-forming VSC control strategy when connected to a weak grid considering the ability of symmetrical and asymmetrical faults ride-through is studied in this paper. The general control scheme is based on the grid-forming direct voltage control to work as a controlled AC voltage source by regulating the active and reactive power delivering to the AC grid. A voltage balancing control loop is proposed to overcome the limited overcurrent capability of the direct voltage control based grid-forming VSC during AC faults. To provide individual control for positive- and negative-sequence current, the control system is based on the double synchronous reference frames. A dq current distribution control is developed to share the positive-sequence active and reactive current, while a negative-sequence current control is proposed to control the negative-sequence active and reactive current in the event of an asymmetrical fault. Simulation results are presented to confirm the feasibility of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Threshold virtual impedance current limiting design for grid-forming converters considering voltage vector location
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: Threshold virtual impedance (TVI) is a promising current limiting technology to ensure the hardware integrity of grid-forming converters (GFMs), as it maintains the voltage source characteristic behind an impedance. Existing TVI parameter design principles are based on limiting the GFM current to a maximum value when a bolted fault is applied at the point of common coupling (PCC). However, adopting existing TVI parameter design practices can cause the GFM current to exceed the maximum value after a fault is cleared, or under a large grid phase jump, since the angular difference between the GFM internal and PCC voltage vector can be large, causing the voltage across the virtual impedance and output transformer to exceed that assumed for TVI parameter design. Hence, the worst case design scenario is not during a fault, but during the subsequent recovery period, or under a large phase jump. Here, a new TVI parameter design process is proposed based on the GFM internal voltage vector being in anti-phase to the PCC voltage vector. However, the new approach should not be applied directly as the GFM current capacity may not be fully used. Hence, three alternative strategies are proposed, with a combined approach being recommended based on electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulations for a range of case studies.

articleTitle: Equivalent modelling for multi-boundary interconnected grid with renewable energy based on improved reinforcement learning
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: The methods for determining the equivalent model of interconnected power grid with multi-boundary nodes, including renewable energy, has become essential due to the rapid growth of distributed renewable energy and regional interconnected power grid. In this paper, an equivalent method is developed for multi-boundary nodes interconnected power grid containing wind and solar renewable energy, based on a parallel multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithm. Changes in renewable energy generation and power flow conditions significantly impact the parameters of the equivalent model in the context of network equivalence. Therefore, we adopt a piecewise equivalent method based on the ternary joint probability distribution of wind-solar-load, which increases the equivalent modelling accuracy of the grid compared with the traditional uniform piecewise method. An improved parallel multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithm is proposed, which parallelizes the decision-making behavior of agents and adjusts the update strategy of reward function and value function. Compared with the traditional multi-agent reinforcement learning and genetic algorithm, it shows higher computational efficiency and accuracy. The feasibility and superiority of the proposed method are demonstrated through a simulation test on an interconnected power grid between UAE and Oman.

articleTitle: Universal modelling and analysis of grid-scale electrolysers frequency response in wind-dominated power systems
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: Integrating hydrogen technologies such as electrolysers could provide frequency support to renewable energy-dominated power systems while also ensuring the production of green hydrogen. This study aims to improve the frequency performance of wind-dominated power systems by investigating the implementation of grid-scale electrolyser plants to provide frequency stability support. Firstly, a universal system frequency response (SFR) model is proposed, which allows for high accuracy compared to the full-order model and requires low computation time. The electrolyser plant power-tracking response model and its proposed control strategies for frequency regulation are then integrated into this improved SFR model. Finally, a modified IEEE 39-bus system with 50% wind penetration is used to evaluate the capability of large-scale electrolyser plants to provide frequency support using different control strategies and electrolyser types. It is found that the proposed RoCoF-based droop control and virtual inertia controller can significantly improve the system frequency response during an extreme power disturbance. Additionally, due to its slow response characteristic, the alkaline electrolyser plant negatively impacts the electrolyser plant frequency support ability.

articleTitle: Experimental investigations into common mode impedance of PV panels
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: The nature of common mode (CM) parasitic impedance (Z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">PV</sub>) of photovoltaic (PV) panels is investigated by experimentation. Measurements are done by two methods: (a) time domain signal recording using a signal generator and an oscilloscope (b) frequency sweep using an LCR meter. It is shown that Z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">PV</sub> is not purely capacitive for the frequency range from 50 Hz to 1 MHz. It is also shown that the total common mode impedance in a PV installation is affected by the nature of Z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">PV</sub>. The frequency spectrum of CM current would be different if Z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">PV</sub> is not purely capacitive. This would affect the design of CM filters on the DC and AC side and also equipment like PV emulators, DC line impedance stabilization network, etc.

articleTitle: Optimal planning of renewable-based community energy system for island-mode operation during prolonged outages
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: Energy communities are emerging as important local actors to help accelerate decarbonisation of the energy sector. By increasing uptake of distributed generation from renewable energy sources, energy communities can take advantage of the benefits provided by local clean energy usage in different ways. In this context, this paper presents a strategy for optimal planning of renewablebased community energy systems for island-mode operation during prolonged outages. The proposed method is formulated as a mixed-integer quadratic problem aimed at minimising the expected energy not supplied subject to operating constraints of the network and resource constraints on the number of distributed generation units that can be installed in the network. Furthermore, it is demonstrated in a realistic network model using representative datasets of renewable energy and load demand profiles in Bristol, UK.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of VSC based control strategy for a large-scale grid connected PV system and harmonics analysis under sudden changes in weather conditions
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: Photovoltaic based power generation is considered as one of the most economic renewable resources in fight against climate change. To this end, an exponential increase has been observed in recent years for installation of grid connected photovoltaic systems (GCPV). However, these systems are highly dependent on weather conditions and should be provided with the effective control system for successful and sustainable operation. In this paper a MATLAB/Simulink based dynamic model of a large-scale GCPV system with power capacity of 2MW is developed. A control system is designed for successful operation of the PV system to operate at maximum delivery point under changing weather conditions. Perturb and observation (P&O) algorithm based maximum power point technique is applied for maximum power extraction at all operating points and Voltage source converter (VSC) based control systems is configured for its integration with the grid. A LC filter is tuned for varying operating conditions and interfaced with inverter for harmonics compensation. The performance of the control strategy is validated by applying sudden changes in weather conditions and monitoring voltage regulation and dynamic response of the system. Moreover, Fast Fourier Transformation (FFT) analysis is performed for all cases to validate the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) level in accordance with the grid standards.

articleTitle: New indices for voltage sags in distribution systems
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: One of the main characteristics of the smart grid is the availability of detailed and continuous measurements, taken with high resolution at various points of the distribution system. Leveraging the quantity and quality of information that can be extracted by such recording, this paper proposes a set of new indices to characterise voltage sags in distribution systems. These indices are currently evaluated and proposed to be included in the next revision of IEEE Standard 1564, but they may be also adopted by other standardisation bodies across the world. Accurate characterisation of voltage sags will allow for a more accurate monitoring of the grid behaviour, and will be a useful tool for power system operators and customers.

articleTitle: Distribution network forecasting and utilisation monitoring
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: The transition to electrify heat and transport to meet the climate change targets set by the UK government is driving a significant increase in the use of Low Carbon Technologies (LCT) such as electric vehicles and heat pumps. This, in turn, will result in an unprecedented increase in demand growth on the electricity networks across the UK. Distribution network operators (DNOs) play a critical role in facilitating this transition by creating additional capacity on the network and maintaining high levels of network reliability and resilience. In this paper, a planning approach is presented that aims to identify areas that need to be reinforced within the primary distribution network. Steps of data cleansing, forecasting, and assessing network loading are presented that consider LCT impact on network peak demand. This methodology has been adopted by NIE Networks in developing load-related reinforcement investment plans for the primary network as part of RP7 price control period submission.

articleTitle: Chance-constrained energy dispatch of railway smart power systems considering uncertainty of traction load
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: Railway smart power systems (RSPSs) integrated with power flow controllers (PFC) and energy storage (ES) have shown to effectively manage peaks and valleys in railway traction loads, and improve the utilization of energy. However, concerns over the efficiency operation of RSPSs under uncertainty challenge have been raised. In this paper, a stochastic optimal operation model is established, which sets the minimum daily operation energy cost, the control scheme of PFC and charging/discharging strategy of ES as decision variables, and uncertainty of traction load is treated as a chance-constrained power flow condition. The case study results show that the proposed optimal energy dispatch can release 32% of the operating cost under uncertain conditions.

articleTitle: Modelling of inertia characteristic of grid-forming VSCs and analysis of its impact on grid frequency
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: This paper proposes a frequency-domain modelling and analysis method to study grid frequency dynamics with grid-forming converters (GFCs). In this paper, the equivalent inertia of the GFC is illustrated based on the swing motion equation model of GFCs, which becomes a transfer function rather than a constant value like traditional synchronous generators, and behaves as time-varying characteristic. Then an aggregation model is deduced and the bode-diagram analysis method is proposed to study grid frequency dynamics with GFCs. In the proposed method, the zero crossing and phase margin of the bode diagram is used to evaluate the change rate and the nadir of grid frequency with the transfer-function-based inertia coefficient. A case study is used to validate the effectiveness and correctness of the proposed method in this paper.

articleTitle: Design of high voltage DC transformers for large scale new energy transmission
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: The use of DC/DC converters to achieve full DC transmission of large-scale new energy can improve the operational efficiency and safety stability of the system. This paper proposes a new type of DC/DC converter to address the low engineering feasibility of current high-voltage and high-capacity DC/DC converters. Firstly, the topology construction theory based on auxiliary branch construction and the basic working principle of the new converter are introduced. Secondly, a two-phase bridge arm energy balance control strategy was proposed that can achieve stable power transmission and voltage transformation. And the parameter design method of the proposed transformer was introduced. Finally, the stable operation of the proposed transformer was simulated and verified on the PSCAD simulation platform, verifying the effectiveness of the proposed topology, control strategy, and parameter design method, providing theoretical support for the engineering application of high-voltage high-capacity DC/DC converters.

articleTitle: Technical and economic analysis of different transmission schemes of far-offshore wind power
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: Far-offshore has a wider sea area, larger wind energy reserves and higher quality wind resources, which is an important direction for the future development of wind power. However, with the increasing capacity and area of far-offshore wind farms, the technical and economic problems of far-offshore wind power transmission are becoming more prominent and there is an urgent need for an in-depth analysis of the cost of various far-offshore wind power transmission schemes. Thus, this paper compiles the typical transmission schemes of modular multilevel converter-based high voltage direct current (MMC-HVDC) transmission, low-frequency AC transmission, and full direct current collection and transmission (Full DC) for far-offshore wind power, and proposes a life-cycle cost assessment method by combining the initial investment cost, operation and maintenance cost. Typical cases are selected to construct the topologies of three transmission schemes, and the life cycle economic indexes and transmission distances of these schemes are analysed and compared. Considering a 25-year life cycle, under the case conditions of 1000MW capacity and 100km transmission distance, the total cost of the MMC-HVDC transmission scheme is the highest, followed by the low-frequency transmission scheme, and the full DC transmission scheme is the lowest, saving about 16% cost compared with the MMC-HVDC transmission scheme.

articleTitle: Outer loop control design of grid-forming converters for enhanced transient stability and current limiting capability
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: Current limiting is necessary to ensure the hardware integrity of grid-forming converters (GFMs), but with implications for the grid-forming ability itself. Implementing a threshold virtual impedance (TVI) is a promising current limiting technology, as it maintains the voltage source characteristic behind an impedance. In this paper, a new P̃/f droop control is proposed to enhance the transient stability of a droop control-based GFM under TVI current limiting control for large fault events, which is achieved by replacing the real-time active power, P, with a modified value, P̃, whereby the voltage drop caused by the TVI control is not included. Existing work has demonstrated that the virtual impedance ratio, σVIX/R, has a conflicting effect on system dynamics and transient stability, i.e. a small σVIX/R results in a well-damped current response, but a very limited transient stability margin, while a large σVIX/R results in a poorly-damped current response, but an acceptable transient stability margin. Under the proposed P̃/f droop control, this dilemma is avoided, i.e. a small σVIX/R not only results in a well-damped current response, but also further enhances the transient stability. Finally, since the standard dispatchable virtual oscillator control (dVOC)-based GFM doesn't incorporate current limiting control, here, the same TVI current limiting control (again, a small σVIX/R is recommended for fault events) is added to the outer control loop of the original dVOC-based GFMs, such that the above P̃/f droop characteristic is provided for a dVOC-based GFM.

articleTitle: Transient stability analysis and modelling of systems with grid-forming converters and synchronous generators
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: The transient stability of a power system with both grid-forming converters (GFMs) and synchronous generators (SGs) under large faults is rarely reported. This paper finds out that even when a SG and GFM have the same frequency during a fault by setting the same inertia and damping coefficient for both, due to the impact of the dynamics of the SG field and amortisseur flux linkage, a parallel connected GFM with low capacity ratio between the GFM and SG outputs negative postfault active power. In other words, the GFM becomes synchronization unstable according to traditional definition. Since normally a GFM has much larger damping (to have strong robustness during small and large disturbances), this negative active power is even lower and lasts longer in practical cases. When conducting transient stability analysis, existing methods usually model a GFM in the same form as the classic SG model, and did not provide theoretical analysis. To simplify analysis and facilitate control design under large disturbances, this paper adopts a modal analysis-based model order reduction technique and finds out that while a GFM can be modelled as the classic form together with the virtual impedance current limiting control, the interacted SGs should not be modelled in the classic form, because the SG field and amortisseur flux linkage should also be included. Finally, this paper finds that for systems with only GFMs as voltage sources, reserving only the dynamics of the voltage angle control loop of GFMs is precise enough for representing the system low-frequency oscillations phenomenon.

articleTitle: Evaluation of type 5 synchronous wind power plants in power systems with high non-synchronous renewable shares
publicationTitle: Renewable Power Generation and Future Power Systems Conference 2023 (RPG 2023 UK)
abstract: In recent years, the increasing integration of non-synchronous renewables into power systems has raised concerns about stability and system services. This has led to increased recognition of the importance of "grid-forming" capabilities for future generation and storage technologies. One such promising technology is the Type 5 hydrostatic transmission-based wind turbine (HSWT), which combines a hydrostatic transmission with a directly grid-connected synchronous generator. Consequently, Type 5 HSWTs benefit from the advantages of synchronous machines, including fault current support, inertial response, and voltage support. Moreover, incorporating a hydraulic accumulator for short-term energy storage further enhances the system service capabilities of Type 5 HSWTs. This paper investigates the integration of Type 5 wind power plants and provides detailed modelling, control strategies, case studies on reliability services and system stability using the IEEE 14-bus system, and an evaluation of their performance, advantages, and limitations.
